equity.level_reason: Clinic-reported canine vaccination results are given separately for rural-county and affected-city clinics and described (rural clinics recommend more, with higher owner compliance), but not framed as a disparity or quantified as a contrast.

level_alternative.reason: The rural vs city split is really outbreak-affected vs unaffected geography about dogs' vaccination, not a social position of people; occupation is a route of exposure, not SES.

equity.equity_measurement: Rurality is a clinic-level label (rural counties vs the affected city) from a small voluntary survey (6 of 10 city clinics, 8 rural clinics) reporting estimated percentages of dogs and owners.

notes: Data focus is yes on the basis of outbreak case counts and the pre/post vaccination survey; a stricter reading is limited (one human case with context). NEDSS was used only for case finding, so it is not listed as a source. No statistical tests or models are reported, so procedures is empty. [review] Other fields of the structural record are acceptable; data_focus 'yes' is defensible given the 13-dog case series and the pre/post clinic survey.
